subject: Follow-up: MedX audit artifacts (who/when) — sample export & retention
thread_preview: Next steps and sample format for who/when access export; requested retention and residency info.
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@medxhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: MedX audit artifacts (who/when) — sample export & retention

Hi Asha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps on the audit/loging artifacts you asked about (we captured this live but want to put the plan in writing):

Summary from call:
- Use case: security & compliance team needs a ‘who/when’ export covering user activity and model access for the past 13 months for a subset of production traffic (initial proof-of-concept).
- Primary asks: sample export format (CSV preferred), column list, timezone normalization, retention policy confirmation, and proof-of-delivery for your audit team.

Questions we need you to confirm so we scope the sample correctly:
1) Which minimum fields must appear in the sample? (timestamp, actor, actor_email, resource_id, action, model_version, request_id, ip_address, workspace_id are options)
2) Do you need obfuscated PII (email redaction/pseudonymization) in the sample, or can we deliver real email addresses for matched users?
3) For residency: should the export be restricted to US-only data centers, or do you need EU residency for the sample?
4) Preferred file format: CSV with UTF-8 + header row, or NDJSON?

Planned next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll produce a 1,000-row CSV sample (who/when slice) and an export spec doc by Friday (6/18).
- If you confirm masking/PII rules, we’ll apply pseudonymization to email fields and provide a mapping key under NDA if required.
- Provide MD5 checksum and a short readme describing columns and any normalization.

I attached a quick template (medx_who_when_sample.csv) with header suggestions — we’ll replace the content with live examples once you confirm the field list and masking approach.

Can you confirm answers to Q1–Q4 above and whether the security@medxhealth.com alias should be included on delivery?

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183
Redwood Inference

Attachment: medx_who_when_sample.csv (template, header-only)

From: Asha Rao <asha@medxhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medxhealth.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedX audit artifacts (who/when) — sample export & retention

Thanks Soojin — great recap. Answers below: 

Q1: Our compliance team requires these fields at minimum: timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), user_id (internal, numeric), user_email, action (e.g., 'view', 'generate', 'download'), resource_type (model/endpoint), resource_id, request_id, model_version, response_size_bytes, source_ip, user_agent.
Q2: For the sample (POC) we prefer real email addresses so we can map to our identity directory, but we will require pseudonymization for the full production export. The sample will be covered by the NDA we signed.
Q3: Residency: for now US-only is fine for the sample. We will want EU residency for production later (we'll flag that in the security questionnaire).
Q4: CSV (UTF-8) with a header row is preferred. Please normalize timestamps to UTC.

A couple additional asks:
- Can you include the event type taxonomy in the readme (how you classify 'generate' vs 'api_call' vs 'system')?
- Retention: our policy asks for 13 months accessible, then archived 2 years. For the POC sample, only the 13-month slice is needed.

If you can deliver the sample and spec by Friday, we'll route to our SOC team for an initial review. Include security@medxhealth.com on delivery.

Best,
Asha Rao
Head of Compliance Programs | MedX Health
asha@medxhealth.com

---
On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 03:12 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@medxhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: MedX audit artifacts (who/when) — sample export & retention

Looping in a quick technical plan and open questions from the infra side. I attached export_spec_v1.json with field types and a suggested CSV header order. Summary:
- We can produce a 1,000-row sample CSV normalized to UTC with the exact fields Asha listed.
- PII handling: for POC we'll include real user_email in the sample under NDA; for production export we’ll support SHA256-salted pseudonyms and a separate mapping file delivered under locked storage.
- Residency: we'll scope the export job to US regions for this sample. For EU residency we’ll propose a private deployment or dedicated tenancy in an EU region for production exports.

Open items for Soojin to confirm with the customer:
1) Do they need request payloads included (we usually exclude full prompt text for privacy; we can include a truncated hash).
2) Are there any regulatory IDs or redaction requirements beyond email (SSN, MRN)?
3) Confirm exact retention lifecycle (13 months accessible then archive) and archive format (compressed Parquet or flat CSV).

Planned deliverables and ETA:
- export_spec_v1.json (attached) — EOD 6/18
- 1k-row medx_who_when_sample.csv — EOD 6/18
- delivery_timeline.xlsx (high-level milestones & owner) — EOD 6/18

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: export_spec_v1.json (field types & sample schema)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@medxhealth.com>, security@medxhealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedX audit artifacts (who/when) — sample export & retention

Asha — thanks for the quick responses. We’ll proceed as follows based on the plan below. Deliverables will be uploaded to the Drive link and a notification will be sent to security@medxhealth.com: 

Deliverables (target: Fri 6/18 EOD PT):
- medx_who_when_sample.csv (1k rows, UTC timestamps, header as requested)
- export_spec_v1.json (field types and event taxonomy)
- delivery_timeline.xlsx (milestones: sample -> SOC review -> production run)
- README.md (checksums, normalization notes, PII handling notes)

PII & retention notes:
- Sample will include real user_email under NDA. Production exports will use salted SHA256 pseudonyms by default unless MedX requests otherwise.
- Retention lifecycle will be: 13 months hot storage (queryable), then 24 months archived (read-only compressed Parquet) unless you instruct a different policy.

Next steps for MedX (Asha):
- Confirm whether you want request payload hashes included in the sample (we’ll include rho-truncated SHA256 hashes of prompts if you want)
- Confirm any additional redaction rules or regulatory IDs to strip before delivery

We’ll upload to: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/medx-audit-specs and send a HubSpot note under deal MX-2027-0451 once uploads complete.

If that all looks good, we’ll push the sample by EOD and schedule a short sync early next week with your SOC reviewers.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: delivery_timeline.xlsx, medx_who_when_sample.csv, export_spec_v1.json
